Africa, 1910; accompanied General Beyers, commandant general of Union cuzz forces on mission to attend military manoeuvres and inspect military institutions in England, Switzerland, France and Germany, 1912; published for some years "Het Zuid Afrikaanse Jaarboek"; author of first sketch of practical plan for Union of South Africa, 1907; edited for publication "Minutes of the South African National Convention," 1911.

HOGGEN, GEORGE, C.M.G. (1915).—B. 1855; M.A., F.G.S.; gold medallist, R.G.S.; stud. at Congregational School, Lewisham, Univ. School, Nottingham, and Cambridge Univ.; mathematical scholar and prizeman, St. Catherine's coll., Cambridge; 1st class hon. in maths.; served in accountant and controller gen.'s dept., Inland Revenue, London, 1872-3; second master, boys' high school, Christchurch, New Zealand, 1881-1889; inspr. of schls., North Canterbury, 1887-1889; headmstr., Timaru high schl., 1889-1899; inspr. gen. of schls. and head. educ'tn. dept., New Zealand, 1899; represented N.Z. at Education Conference in London, 1907.

HOGG, ALAN F.—B. 1868; ed. at Winchester and King's Coll., Camb.; 2nd cls. hist. tripos, 1890; 2nd cls. law tripos, 1891; prizeman of the coun. of legal educ. in common law and equity, 1891; Whewell scholar of international law, 1893; called to the Bar, Inner Temp., 1892; stip. mag., Entebbe, admistr.gen., prin. registrar of documents, and register of companies, Uganda Prot., 6th Nov., 1908; atty-gen., Nyassaland, 1914.
HOGUE, Hon. James Alexander.—B. 1846; M.L.A. for The Glebe, New S. Wales since 1894; min. of pub. instr. and min. for labour, 1898-9; col. sec., 1904-7; min. of pub. instr. and min. for labour, 1907-1910.

HOLDEN, George.—Asst. supt. of wks., S. Stltlms., June, 1901; supt. of wks., Prov. Wellesley, Jan., 1908; ag. supt. of wks. and surveys, Singapore, July, 1908; ditto, Malacca, May, 1909; exec. engrnr., Malacca, Dec., 1909.

HOLLAND, Bernard H., C.B. (1904).—B. 1856; ed. at Eton and Trin. Coll.; Camb.; called to bar, Inner Temp., 1882; in office of charity comsn., 1884-1890; priv. sec. to Duke of Devonshire, 1892-1894; sec. to royal comsn. on financial relations between Great Britain and Ireland, 1894-1896; to Lt. Rothschild's comttee. on old-age pensions, 1896-1898; to Transvaal concessions comsn., 1900-1901; to royal comsn. on Port of London, 1901-2; and to royal comsn. on war in S. Africa, 1902-3; priv. sec. to Right Hon. Alfred Lyttelton, S. of S. for the colonies, 1903; ditto to Lord Elgin, 1905-1908; author of "Imperium et Libertas," etc.

HOLLAND, J.—B. 1838; apptd. after exam., 3rd cl. messenger, C.O., 18th Aug., 1902; 2nd cl. ditto, 10th June, 1904; 1st cl. messenger, 30th Jan., 1912.

HOLLIMAN, J. W., I.S.O. (1912).—Served in Impl. treasury; entd. civ. ser., New South Wales, Mar., 1884; served as sec. to pub. ser. board; under-sec. for finance and trade, Jan., 1907.

HOLLINGSWORTH, A. H.—A.M. Inst. C.E.; ed. King's Coll., London, engineering dept.; art. pupil, borough and water engrnr., Croydon; asst. engrnr. to borough and water engrnr., Croydon; asst. engrnr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, Dec., 1896; ag. exec. engrnr. in charge of water and drain. wks., Aug., 1900; ag. consulting sanitary survr., Sept., 1900; exec. engrnr. in charge of water and drain wks., 1st Jan., 1902; J.P., 1907.

HOLLIS, Alfred Claud, C.M.G. (1911).—Ed. Highgate and St. Leonards, and in Switzerland and Germany; asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 12th Mar., 1897; collr., 15th June, 1900; ag. Brit. vice-consul for German East Africa, Apr., 1900, to Feb., 1901; ag. sec. to admtn. and priv. sec. to H.M. comsnr. from Feb., 1901, to Apr., 1903; sec. to the admtn., 1st Apr., 1903; sec. for native affairs, 13th June, 1907; African general serv. medal, Jubaland and Nardi (1905-6) clasps; ag. chief sec. to gov't., Apr. to Dec., 1911 and Feb. to Oct., 1912; col. sec., Sierra Leone, 1912.

HOLLIS, Herbert.—Assoc. M. Inst. C.E.; supt., P.W.D., Jamaica, Mar., 1894, to Jan., 1913; colonial engrnr., Gambia, Feb., 1913; P.R. and comsnr. of court of requests.

HOLM, Alexander.—M.R.A.S.E., F.H.A.S., S.E.A.C.; gen. manager, govt. experimental farm, Potchefstroom, Transvaal, 1903; gen. manager and principal, schl. of agric., Potchefstroom, 1908; under sec. for agric. (educt.), Union of S. Africa, Oct., 1912.

HOLMAN, Hon. W. A.—Barrister-at-law; M.L.A., New South Wales, since 1898; chmn. of elections qualifications comttee, 1904; atty.-gen. and min. of justice, Oct., 1910; atty.-gen., Apl., 1912; premier, col. sec. and atty.-gen., June, 1913; premier and col. treas., 1914.

Holme, Henry Frederick.—4th clk., col. sec.'s office, Antigua, Leeward Islands, 1898; ag. 3rd clk., 1898 and 1900; ag. priv. sec., 1900 and 1901; ag. 2nd clk., 1900 and 1905; 2nd clk., 1901; supht., printing office, 1905; ag. asst. col. sec., 1906, 1907, 1908 and 1909; clk., legis. coun., Antigua, 1908; priv. sec. to ag. gov., Apr. to Nov., 1909.

Holmes, John Richard.—S.S.C., 1879; barrister, Mid. Tem., 1889; dist. comsnr., G. Coast, 1889; commanded detachment in Woonahoon exdpn., 1889-91; pres. dist. ct., Cyprus, 1899.

HOLROYD, Sir Edward Dundas, Kt. B.A.C. (1903).—B. 1828; ed. at Winchester (Queen's gold medal for Latin and English essays), Trin. Coll. Camb. (B.A. 1st cls. tripos, 1851, M.A., 1854); student, Gray's Inn, 1851; called to the bar, 1855; called to Victorian bar, 1859; Tasmanian bar, 1867; Q.C., 1879; raised to bench, Aug., 1881; ex-pres. of Impl. Fed. League of Victoria; sen. puisne judge of sup. ct. of Victoria; ret. 1st Aug., 1906.

Holt, Thomas Herbert.—B. 1861; ed. at Fulneck Schl., Yorks; entd. office of Messrs. J. and B. Freeland, Crown Agents' shipping agents, 1876; senr. partner, 1909; head of Crown Agents shipping office, 1912.

Holtze, Maurice Wm., I.S.O. (1913), F.L.S., etc.—Govt. gardener, Port Darwin, 1878; botanic gardener, 1880; dir. botanic garden, Adelaide, 1891.

Homagee, James Francis, I.S.O. (1906).—Court messenger, St. Helena, 1859; clk. to ch. just., 1862; man. govt. savings bk., 1863; clk. of the peace, taxing master, and registr. sup. ct., 1867; legal adviser, crown prosecutor, and registr. V.-A. ct., 1870; also supervisor of customs and registr. of shipping, in 1883; admity. advoc., 1890.

Homburg, Hermann.—Mem. of H. of A., South Australia, since 1906; atty.-gen., 1909-1910; atty.-gen. and min. of industry, 1912.

Honey, John Wm., C.M.G. (1908).—Served under Cape govt., 1880 to 1901; transfld. to Transvaal when collr. and prin. controller of cust. and prin. registr. of shipping; served in Gaika-Galeka and Basutoland campaigns, holding comsnr. in latter as lieut. Capetown Rifles; dir. of cust., Transvaal, and cust. adviser to high comsnr., 16th May, 1901; M.L.C., Mem. I.C.C.; chrmn., tender and post office investment boards; ag. sec. for commerce and industries, and ag. comsnr. of customs and excise, Union of S. Africa, 1910; retired, 1911.

Honey, De Symons Montagu George.—Served in B.S.A. Co.'s expedit. to Mashonaland, 1891 to 1893; with B. C. Africa admtn., 1893 to 1896; cust. dept., Transvaal, 9th Apr., 1901; native affairs dept., 1902; sec. for Swaziland affairs, and actng. offr., 20th Oct., 1904; govt. sec., Swaziland admtn., 22nd Mar., 1907.

HOOD, Hon. Joseph Henry.—B. 1846; M.A.; puisne judge, Victoria, since 1890.

HOOD, Thos.—Ed. City of London, schl., Univ. Coll., and St. Bart.'s hosp., London; M.R.C.S., Eng.; L.R.C.P., Lond.; asst. col. surg., S. Leone, 1897; served on staff during native rising, 1898 (W. African medal and clasp, 1898); comsnr. of Bandajuma dist., 1899; senior med. offr., 1902; ag. prin. med. offr., Oct. 1903, to Mar., 1904; J.P. for the colony; acted as P.M.O. and M.O.H. on three occasions during 1903 to 1907 for a total period of twenty months; transfld. as sen. med. offr., Gambia, Mar., 1907; chmn., bd. of health, 1907; dep. P.M.O., S. Nigeria, 1911; P.M.O., S. Nigeria, 12th June, 1913.

HOOD, Hon. Victor Albert Nelson.—B. 1862; priv. sec. to gov. of S. Aust. (Sir G. le Huntel), 1903; priv. sec. to gov. of Victoria (Sir R. Talbot), 1906; priv. sec. to gov's. of Victoria (Sir T. G. Carmichael), 1908, and Sir John Fuller, 1911; priv. sec. to Sir Gerald Strickland,
as gov. of W. Australia and New South Wales, 1912-13; chamberlain to Lord Denman, gov. gen. of Australia, 1911, and priv. sec. to govrs. of Victoria (Sir John Fuller) 1913-14, and Sir Arthur Stanley, 1914.

HOOPER, JAMES.—B. 1855; ed. parochial schools, Hatherleigh, Devonshire; journalist, and manager of newspapers in Canada; dep. prov. sec. and King's printer, Manitoba, 1900; is a J.P.; now king's printer.

HOOPS, ALBERT LAUNCELOT.—B. 1876; ed. at King William's Coll. and Trinity Coll., Dublin; B.A., 1900; M.B., B.Ch., B.A.O., 1901; M.D. (stip. cond.) 1903; D.P.H., 1903; L.M., Rotunda, 1903; certif. honours, London Schl. of Trop. Med., 1904; served in S. African War as medical offir., 28th M.I., 1901-2 (severely wounded, ment. in desps., medal and four clasps); house surgeon, Penang, 1904; surg. capt., Penang vols.; ag. col. surx. res., Penang, June, 1905; seconded to organise medical and prison dept., Kedah, Mar., 1906; state surg. and supt. of prisons in Kedah since that date; ag. adviser to govt. of Kedah, Sept., 1906, to Apr., 1907, and from July to Oct., 1907; supt. of Indian immigts., Kedah, in addition to other duties, Oct., 1910.

HOPE, JAMES WILLIAM.—B. 1851; med. offir., convict estabt., Fremantle; med. supt., invalid depot; med. offir., native penal settlement, Rottnest Is.; and health offir., Port of Fremantle, W. Australia, July, 1884; dist. med. offir. and quarantine offir., Fremantle, 1895; major, Aust. field artillery.

HOPE, JOHN OWEN WEBLEY.—3rd treasy. asst., E. Africa Prot., 17th May, 1899; asst. collr., 1st Apr., 1900; collr., 1st Apr., 1903.

HOPKINS, F. F.—Chief clk., secretariat, N. Nigeria, 16th Oct., 1901; confil. clk. to high consmr., 1st Apr., 1902; priv. sec., 11th Dec., 1902; title changed to asst., high consmr.'s office, 1903; chief asst., high consmr.'s office, 12th Feb., 1904; ag. polit. asst., and chief asst. from 1st Apr., 1907; is now titled chief asst. polit. sec.; holds S. Africa medal with 3 clasps, and W. Africa gen. ser. medal, with clasp "N. Nigeria, 1903."

HOPKINS, FRANCIS GETHIN.—Ed. Trin. Coll., Dublin, B.A., M.D., etc.; asst. col. surg., Lagos, 1894; sen. asst. col. surg., 1897; sen. med. offir., W.A.M.S., 1902; dep. P.M.O., 1906; has acted as P.M.O. since 1897; M.L.C., Aug., 1903, to Feb., 1904; chmn., infant mortality consmr., 1901; prin. med. offir., G. Coast, 1911; mem. exec. and legis. couns.

HOPKINSON, EMILIUS, D.S.O., M.A., M.B., B.Ch. (Oxon.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), F.Z.S.—B. 1869; ed. at Haileybury, Trin. Coll., Oxford, and St. Thomas's hosp., Lond.; late ophthalmic house surg., St. Thomas's hosp.; clinical asst., Royal Ophthalmic hosp., Moorfields; house surg., Radcliffe infirmary, Oxford; served in S. African war, 1900-1901, as surg.-capt., 15th batt., I.Y. (ment. in desps., D.S.O.); late surg.-lieut., Oxford I.Y.; med. offir., W.A.F.F., Gambia, 1901-1902; prot. med. offir., Gambia, 1903.

HOIPLEY, WILLIAM MUSGROVE.—B.A. (Can. tab.), 1878; b. 1833; called to bar (Inner Temple), 1878; joined Cape sup. ct. bar, 1878; ag. crown prosecutor (Griqualand W.), July, 1885; crown prosecutor (Griqualand W.), Feb., 1886; Q.C., 1890; a judge of the Cape sup. ct. and assigned to the high court of Griqualand, Mar., 1892; assigned to sup. ct. temporarily, 1904-1907, and permanently, 1st July, 1907.

HOPTROFF, WALLACE FRANK.—B. 1872; examir. of acts., repatriation dept., O.R.C., 2nd Jan., 1903; acctnt., govt. relief dept., 1st Jul., 1903; acctnt. repatriation recoveries branch, treasy., 1st July, 1905; cashier, treasy., 2nd Oct., 1906.

HOPWOOD, RT. HON. SIR FRANCIS JOSEPH STEPHENS, P.C. (1912).—G.C.M.G. (1896), K.C.B. (1901), K.C.M.G. (1906), C.B. (1886), C.M.G. (1893).—B. 1860; ed. at Louth by Capt. W. W. Hopwood; admitted a solr., 1882; asst. lawclk., B. of T., 1885-1888; asst. solr., 1888-1892; priv. sec. to pres. of B. of T., 1892; sec. rly. dept., 1892-1901; perm. sec., 1901; perm. under-secr. of S. for the colonies, 1907-1910; employed on different occasions upon offl. missions to U.S.A., Canada, and Newfoundland; Bt. deleg. to internat. rly. congress in London, 1892; and in Paris, 1900; hon. sec. to chmn. of select comttee. of H. of C. on Jameson raid, 1897; mem. of London traffic comtn., 1903; visited S. Africa as mem. of Transvaal and O.R.C. constitutions comtn., 1906; mem. of comtn. on canals and waterways, 1906; and on sea freights and shipping "rings," 1906; accompanied H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his visit to Quebec, 1908; mem. of Royal comtn. on electoral reform, 1909; registr. of the Order of St. Michael and St. George, 1907-1909; sec. to Order, 1909-1911; accompanied H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught on his visit to S. Africa in connection with the opening of the first part of the Union of S. Africa, 1910; vice-chmn. of the Development comtn., 1910; specially appd. to act as under sec. of state for the colonies during the period of the Imperial Conf., 1911; additional civil lord of the Admiralty, Jan., 1912.

HORE, ERNEST HENRY.—Entered Impl. post. ser., July, 1871; transfd. to Cyprus for special service, Oct., 1878; entered col. ser., Aug., 1880; asst. to postmnr., Limassol; acted several times as ch. clk.; ch. clk., Feb., 1890; acted several times as Isl. postmnr.; apptd. Isl. postmnr., Apr., 1893.

HORN, ARTHUR EDWIN.—M.D., B.Sc. (Lond.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.); L.R.C.P. (Lond.); D.T.M. & H. (Cantab.); ed. at St. Mary's Hosp. and London Univ.; served as civil surg., 19th brigade field hosp., S. African field force, 1900-1901; apptd. to W. African medical staff, 1904; certif. of London schl. of trop. med. (with distinction); awarded Craggs research prize for original research in trop. med. (London S.T.M.), 1908; recd. thanks of S. of S. for the Colonies for report on cerebro-spinal fever in Northern Territories of the G. Coast, 1908, and for report on sleeping sickness in the Volta River dist. of the G. Coast, 1910; seconded for special service at the C.O., 1910; personal asst. to the P.M.O. S. Nigeria, 24th July, 1912.

HORNYBY-PORTER, CHARLES.—Appld. dist. consmr., Lagos, 1897; 2nd asst. col. sec., 1903; senior asst. col. sec., 1903; ag. col. treas., 1903; ag. col. sec., 1904; holds dormant const. to sit as pol. mag. and sat as such in 1897, 1902 and 1903; on spec. serv. to Jebuwo Ode, 1904 and 1904, and to Oyo and also to Ife, 1904; proc. of pol. consmr., 1901; mem. of rly. consmr., 1901; pres. of cust. consmr., 1904.

HORNE, EDWARD BUTLER.—Ed. at Bedell Gram. Schl.; asst. collr., E. Africa Prot., 2nd Apr., 1904; dist. consmr., 1st Apr., 1909.

HORNE, HENRY HASTINGS.—Ed. at Cliffe Coll.; Brit. vice-consul, Mexico, 1900-01.
frica, field intcl. force, S. African medal; asst. sllr., E. Africa Prot., 3rd Apr., 1903; dist. omsnr., 1st Apr., 1907.

HORSBURGH, B.—B. 1868; M.A. Edin.; det., Ceylon civ. ser., Oct., 1889; attached to le Jaffna Kuchcheri; ag. off. asst., Jaffna, 91; ag. off. asst., Galle, 1893; ag. asst. govt. gent., Vavuniya and Mullaitivu, 1895; agt. vt. agent, Mannar, 1896; asst. govt. agent, ambantota, 1898; asst. govt. agent, Kalutara, 94; off. of cl. II, 11th Mar., 1905; ag. chmn. un. coun., and mayor of Colombo, 1906; govt. gent., N. Cent. Prov., 1908; associated with r. Thurley, of the Madras Presidency salt and kari dept. in introducing an excise system into ceylon, Sept., 1909; seconded for service as ex-seconmr., Sept., 1909; offr. of Cls. I., grade 2, id to remain seconded, Nov., 1910; govt. gt., N.W. Prov., in addition to his own duties, ct. 1910; capt. in Ceylon Arty. Volrs.; had charge of a camp of Boer prisoners of war at ambantota, and served on spec. duty at several arf fish ries since 1891.

HOWOOD, HON. SIR WM. HENRY, KT. BACH. (96).—B. 1862; ed. at Bishop Feild Coll., St. john's; called to the bar, 1886; bencher of the w society, Newfoundland, 1891; Q.C., 1895; elected to the legislature, 1894; acted as col. c. 1894-5; delegate from the Newfoundland wt. to the Ottawa conf., Apr., 1895, on the object of confedn. with Canada; mem. of c. coun., 1894-97; ag. atty.-gen., 1897; elected to legislature to represent Harbour Grace, 1897; apptd. by ch. just., with minister of just. to sit in conjunction with judges as committee to rend rules and procedure, sup. court, 1899; minister of just. and atty.-gen., 1900; ex-officio mem. of ex. coun., and of treasy. board; acted as ader of govt. during sess. of 1901; and also in 92; apptd. ch. just., July, 1902; administered ov't., 1902, 1904, 1905, and 1911.

HOSE, CHARLES, D.SC.—Cadet Sarawak serice, Mar., 1884; res. 2nd cl., div. Jan., 1891; es. 3rd Div., and mem. of sup. coun., May, 904.

HOSKING, E. B.—Asst. dist. comsnr. E.A.P., ec., 1913.

HOSKING, HON. JOHN HENRY.—B. 1854; arrister and solicitor; K.C., 1908; judge of up. ct., New Zealand, 1914.

HOUGHTON, H. E.—B. 1892; apptd. after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser. and assigned to the C.O., Apr., 1912.

HOUSTON, WILLIAM, C.M.G. (1906).—B. 846; formerly under-secr. for lands, N.S. Wales; omsnr. of lands, appeal ct. of N.S. Wales, and deputy admstr. of Norfolk Island, 1899.

HOWARTH, SAMUEL EDWARD JAMES.—Ed. at luxton Coll., London; served in S. African War, queen's and King's medals with five clasps; set. Colony manager, field force canteens, O.R.C., eb., 1902, to Mar., 1903; asst. acctnt., P.W.D., S. Africa Prot., 6th May, 1905.

HOWDEN, HON. JAMES H.—B. 1860; ed. high shls., Rockwood and St. Catherines; barrister-at-law; elect. to the Manitoba legis. for Beautiful lains, 1903, 1907 and 1910; min. of telephones or Manitoba, 1907; prov. sec. 1908; atty.-gen., 01.

HOWELL, AILEYNE GRAHAM.—B. 1871; 5th k. corrpdg. branch, C.S.O., Barbados, 1890; th clk., 1892; 3rd clk., Jan., 1898; ch. clk. omsnr. of agriculture, 1899; sec. to W. Indian agric. conferences, 1900, 1901, 1902, 1905, and 07.

HOWELL, C. G.—Sec. and actuary, Barbados savings bank, 1891.

HOWELL, E. H.—B. 1879; apptd., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser. and assigned to the C.O., Mar., 1898; promoted, with gratuity, Dec., 1907; conf. clk., 1911.

HOWELL, FREDERICK ROUSE.—B. 1886; sup. clk., P.O., Barbados, Feb., 1907; jun. clk., P.O., Nov., 1907; clk. to master in chancery, Dec., 1907; 4th clk., C.S.O., May, 1909.

HOWELL, HON. HECTOR MANSFIELD.—B.1842; ed. pub. schls. and Albert Coll., Ontario; called to the bar, Ontario, 1871; called to the bar, Manitoba, 1879; chief just. of ct. of appeal, Manitoba, 1906; chief just. of Manitoba, 1909.

HOWELL, JOHN BRUCE.—B. 1867; 3rd clk., treasy., Barbados, July, 1886; 3rd clk., col. sec.'s office, Sept., 1891; ag. ch. clk., record branch, C.S.O., Sept., 1893, to Apr., 1894; ag. ch. clk., provost-marshal's office, Dec., 1897, to Apr., 1898; 2nd clk., C.S.O., and clk. of exec. coun. and comtece., Jan., 1898; ag. ch. clk., col. sec.'s office, May to October, 1900; ag. priv. sec. and A.D.C. to the gov. of Barbados, 1st Apr. to 6th July, 1902, and Jan. to Oct., 1904; ag. ch. clk., col. sec.'s off., June to Dec., 1906; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to ag. gov., June to Sept., 1906, and from June to Oct., 1907; ag. priv. sec. and A.D.C. to gov., Mar. to July, 1910, and to ag. gov., July, 1910 to Feb., 1911; ag. priv. sec. to gov., Mar. to July, 1911.

HOY, WILLIAM WILSON.—B. 1868; entd. serv. of Cape Govt. rlys., 1889; representative of C.G.R. in Johannesburg, 1896; ag. asst. traffic manager, Bulawayo, 1897-8; Kimberley, 1898; asst. traffic manager, Port Elizabeth, 1899; traffic manager, Bloemfontein, Johannesburg, 1900; chief traffic manager, C.S.A.R., 1902; represented C.S.A.R. at rly. confce. at Washington; ag. gen. manager in 1905 and 1907; asst. gen. manager, 1909; gen. manager of rlys. and harbours, Union of S. Africa, 31st May, 1910.

HOYLE, HON. H. C.—M.L.A., New South Wales, and hon. M.E.C., 1914.

HUGGINS, HENRY DANIEL.—B. 1856; barrister-at-law, Mid. Temp.; entd. Trinidad service, 1873; clk. of the peace, 1876-80; mag. and warden, Mayaro, 1887; ditto, Cedros, 1894; stip. mag., county of Caroni, 1906.

HUGHES, D.B.B., M.B., C.M. (Edin.).—1st prizeman, senior surgery; medallist, anatomy and pathology; ag. surg. in charge, col. hosp., Grenada, 1900; dist. med. offr., St. Vincent, Dec., 1900.

HUGHES, EDWIN TOM.—B. 1883; ed. Ipswich Sch. and Keble Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1906; off. asst. to govt. agt., N. Prov., Jan., 1908; ag. asst. govt. agt., Mullaitivu, May, 1910; addl. pol. mag. and mun. mag., Colombo, Aug., 1910; ag. pol. mag., Kalutara, Aug., 1911; addtl. pol. mag. and addtl. mun. mag., Colombo, Aug., 1911; asst. govt. agt., Mullaitivu, Nov., 1913.

HUGHES, HON. GEORGE EDWARD.—B. 1854; ed. at Prince of Wales and St. Dunstan's Coll., P.E.I.; a town councillor for eight years; pres., maritime B. of T., P.E.I.; elec. to legis., P.E.I., 1900, 1904, 1908; mem. of exec. coun., without portfolio.

HUGHES, GEORGE ROBERT.—Served in land's and surveys dept., W. Australia; 1897-1901; asst. sec. for lands, Transvaal, 14th July, 1903; under-sec. for lands, July, 1904; sec. for lands, July, 1906; mem. land bd., investment bd.,
townships bd.; sec. for lands and irrigation, 1908; ag. sec. for lands, Union of S. Africa, 31st May, 1910; sec. for lands, 1st Apr., 1912; is a J.P.

HUGHES, Lieut.-R. H. W., R.D., R.N.R.—B. 1872; cadet, H.M.S. "Conway," 1885-87; served in merchant service, 1887-1898; Bd. of T. master mariner's certif.; sub-lieut., R.N.R., 1896; lieut., 1904; 1st class certif. in gunnery, torpedo, signalling and naval training; served in S. African war, in S.A. Light Horse, Bethune's M.I., and Royal Navy, from 12th Dec., 1899 to 1st May, 1902 (2 medals and 8 clasps); served on Major Trenchard's Patrol, S. Nigeria, 1904 (medal and clasp); qualified in surveying at R.G.S. in 1906; elected Younger Brother of Trinity House, 1909; marine offr., S. Nigeria, 27th March, 1903; senr. marine offr., 1st Jan., 1909; ag. marine supt. and harbr.mast., Lagos, 1st July to 10th Dec., 1906; has commanded govt. yacht "Ivy" since 8th March, 1908, during which time has twice reed. special thanks of Lords of Admiralty and S. of S. for hydrographic surveys of coast and rivers of S. Nigeria.

HUGHES, Maj.-Gen. Hon. Samuel.—B. 1853; lecturer, Toronto Coll. Inst. till 1885; journalist, edited Lindsay "Warder"; a volunteer since his 14th year; elected to H. of C., Canada, 1892; re-elec., 1896, 1900, 1904, 1908 and 1911; min. of militia and defence, Oct., 1911; organised Canadian contingents for European war, 1914.

HUGHES, Hon. William Morris.—B. 1864; M.L.A., New South Wales, 1894-1901; elec. to 1st H. of R., C. of A., 1901; re-elec. 1903 and 1906; min. for external affairs, 1904; representative of C. of A. at Navigation Conf., London, 1907; atty.gen., C. of A., Apr., 1910-1913, and since Sept., 1914.

HULL, Hon. H. C.—B. 1860; entd. Cape civ. ser., 1879; left the civ. ser. and practised at the bar for many years; served in S. African war; treasr., Transvaal; min. of finance, Union of S. Africa, 1910-1912.

HULL, H.M., C.M.G. (1902).—B. 1861; ed. at Charterhouse; priv. sec. to gov., G. Coast, and clk. of legis. and exec. couns., May, 1888, to Mar., 1891; travelling comsrr., G. Coast, Mar., 1891; one of the Br. comsrs. for the delimitation of bndry. between the G. Coast Col. and the German Protectorate of Togo, Jan., 1892; ag. dir. of telegraphs, July to November, 1892; apptd. Br. comsrr. to delimit the bndry. between the G. Coast and the Ivory Coast, 1894, the comsrr., however, did not meet; ag. dir. of telegraphs, Aug., 1895, to Feb., 1896; and mentioned in despatches for services during Ashanti expedition, 1895-96; asst. col. sec., G. Coast, Dec., 1899; ag. comptr. of customs, Feb. to June, 1900; on sp. service to E. Akim during Ashanti rising, 1900, raised 3,500 native levies (medal); ag. comptr. of customs, Nov., 1901; sec. for native affairs, Nov., 1902; ret., May, 1907.

HULSE, Leigh Rodwell.—Ed. Belize, Br. Honduras; appren. in gen. registry, Belize, Apr., 1893; copyist, Apr., 1894; 3rd clk., col. sec.'s off., Nov., 1896; 4th clk. treasy. and customs dept. and clk. to the comsrs. of currency, June, 1898; 3rd clk., Sept. 1900; 2nd clk., and clk. to quarantine bd., Dec., 1901; ag. auditor, Apr., 1903; ag. ch. clk., treasy. and cust., 30th May, 1905; ch. clk., Oct., 1905; 2nd lieut. Br. Honds. vol., Aug., 1906; ag. postmr., 16th Jan., 1907; survr. of shipping, Jan., 1907; lieut. Br. Hond. vol., Mar., 1908; A.D.C. to H. E. W. Collet, C.M.G., Nov., 1908; postmr., Apr., 1909; director, pub. offr. guar-

antee fund, Mch., 1910; capt., B. Hond. vol., May, 1911.

HUME, Wm. James Parker.—B. 1866; ed. Haileybury Coll., Bonn-am-Rhein, and Brussel; apptd. to Perak civ. ser., 1888; ag. 4th ass. Kinta, 1889; asst. collr. and mag., Batang Padang, 1890; collr. of land rev., Kinta, 1891; also regis. of titles, Perak South, 1896-7; wrk. of mines, Selangor, 1899; dist. offr., Ulu Palau, 1900; Ulu Selangor, 1901; New Territory, Pen., 1903; Batang Padang, 1904; sen. mag., Pen., 1904-5; sec. to res., Perak, 1905-6; auditor, F.M.S., Nov., 1906; recd. thanks of govt. connection with Ulu Selangor riots in Febr., 1902.

HUMFREY, Capt. Lorn Edward Hambleton.—19th Yorks. Regt., apptd. to Lagos constab., 1st 1894; Ashanti campaign, 1895-6 (star); W. Afr., 1897-8; employed in Lagos Hinterland; attck. Baribas in Borgu country (ment. in despatch); S. Nigeria, 1901-2; Aro exp., 1902 (ment. in despatch); received comms. as cap. Royal Garrison Regt., Sept., 1902; transferred to Yorks. Regt., July, 1905; resident, N. Yor., Oct., 1904; transfd. to S. Nigeria as dist. comm., July, 1906.

HUMPHREYS, John.—Mag. 'clk., Reg., stip. mag., May, 1897.

HUMPHREYS, John Lisseter.—B. 1868; cadet, S. Stlmt., Dec., 1905; dep. coll. distr. rev., and regis. of deeds, Singapore, 21st May, 1906; ag. dist. offr., Alor Gajah, Malacca, 23rd Nov., 1906; passed final exam. in Mat. passed cadet, July, 1907; ag. 4th mag., Pen., Dec., 1909; ag. dist. offr., Dindings, Mar., 1910.

HUMPHRYS, H. L.—Ed. at gram. sch., Antigua; senior Camb. certif., 3rd div. honours; cashier, treasy., Antigua, Jan., 1892; 2nd insp. offr., 1896; ag. 1st indoor offr. on several occasions; ag. ch. audit. clk., Leeward Is., Dec., 1897 to Jan., 1898; ag. audit. clk., St. Kitts-Newf., Dec., 1903, to Mar., 1904; 1st indoor offr. treasy., Antigua, Apr., 1904; ag. ch. audit. and federal acctnt., Leeward Is., Mar. to Oct., 1909, Aug., 1910, and from Apr., 1911 to Feb., 1912; ag. treasr. of Antigua, and federal treas. from Dec., 1912 to Apr., 1913.

HUNT, Atlee Arthur, C.M.G. (1910).—B. 1864; ed. at Balmain pub. schl. and Sydney Gram. schl.; entd. lands dept., New S.W., 1879; resigned in 1887 to study for the bar; admitted to the bar, 1892, and practised until 1900; priv. sec. to first prime min. of C. of A., Jan., 1901; sec. and permanent head of dept. external affairs, C. of A., since 1901; attck. Imp. Conf., 1907 and 1911.

Hunt, Henry Ambrose.—B. 1866; F.R.Met.Soc.; meteorologist, C. of A., 1906.

HUNTER, Lieut.-Gen. Sir Archibald K.C.B. (1898), D.S.O. (1886).—Ed. at Clissold Acad. and Sandhurst; 4th King's Own Reg. Lancaster, 1874; capt., 1882; lieut.-col., 1886; col., 1894; maj.-gen., 1896; served in Egypt twice wounded; gov. of Dongola Prov., commdt. Frontier Field Force, 1893-99; gov. of Omdurman, 1899; Egyptian medal and orders; in command of 1st cls. dist. in Ics. lieut.-gen. on staff, commanded 10th div. S.A.F., 1900-01 (twice ment. in despatch); commandant Scotland, 1901-3; Western Army Corps, 1904-7; commanded Southern Army, 1907-9; gov. and commr.-in-chief, Gibraltar, 1910-1913.

Hunter, Charles Hastings, P. I. (1903).—B. 1864; clk. to audr., St. Le...
HUTCHINSON, Hon. W.—Min. of agric. and water supply, Victoria, Dec., 1913.

HUTCHISON, ROBERT OLIPHANT.—Ed. at Rugby and Hertford Coll., Oxon; cadet, Hong Kong, 1904; ag. asst. registr.-gen., 1907; ag. head of sanitary dept., Nov. 1908 to June, 1909; ag. asst. registr.-gen., July to 29th Oct., 1909; 1st asst. registr.-gen., 30th Oct., 1909; ag. asst. dist. offr., New Territories south, 4th Apr. to 4th July, 1910; supt. of imports and exports, 4th July, 1911.

HUTSON, EYRE, C.M.G. (1911), B.A.—B. 1864; 2nd clk. to gov. Leeward Is., Oct., 1885; asst. priv. sec. to gov. Barbados, Nov., 1885; priv. sec. to gov. Barbados, Mar., 1887; ditto, at Mauritius, Jan., 1890; at Br. Guiana, July, 1893; Jamaica, 1898; apptd. col. sec. and registr.-gen., Bermuda, July, 1901; chrmn., schools comsn., 1902; chrmn., St. George's harbour comsn., 1903; col. sec., Fiji, July, 1908; chrmn., educn. comsn., Apr., 1909; represented Fiji and Western Pacific high comsn., at wireless tel. conf., Melbourne, Dec., 1909; dep.-gov., May and Oct., 1909, Sept., 1910, Mar., Sept., Oct., 1911, and June, 1912.

HUTSON, JOHN, B.A. (Durham) 1879 (2nd cls. honours in class.); M.B., C.M. (Edin.), 1883; D.P.H. (Cantab.), 1905.—B. 1859; res. surg., gen. hosp., Barbados, 1885; sen., ditto, 1886-88; mem. Barbados quarantine comsn., 1903; chrmn. of Glendairy prison comsn., 1903; del. for Barbados at W. Indian quarantine conice., 1904; del. for Barbados on cent. quarantine authority for W. Indies, 1907; poor law inspr., 1901; mem. of bd. of health, 1895, surg.-lieut., Barbados volrs., 1904; surg.-capt., 1906; med. assessor, 1906; ag. M.L.C., 1907.

HUTT, ALAN NORMAN.—B. 1890; B.A. Oxon.; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Dec., 1913; office asst. to gov't. agt., W. Prov., Dec., 1913; addtl. pol. mag., Colombo, in addition to his own duties, Apr., 1914.

HUTTON, EDWARD MALIN, M.A.—Ed. Magdalen Coll. schl.; scholar Queen's Coll., Oxon; 2nd class classical mods., 3rd class final classics; admitted solr., 1870; registr. sup. ct. and ct. of bankruptcy, Gibraltar, 1891; J.P. for Gibraltar, 1892.

HUTTON, MAJ.-GEN. SIR EDWARD THOMAS HENRY, K.C.M.G. (1901); C.B. (1894).—B. 1848; served in the Zulu and Boer wars, 1879-81; Egyptian campaign, 1882; Soudan expeditn., 1884-5; commdg. mounted infantry, and S. African War, 1900-1; raised and commanded M.I. at Aldershot, 1888-92; gen. offr. commdg. forces in N.S. Wales, 1893-6; pres. of mil. conference in Aust., 1896; gen. commdg. Canadian militia, 1898-1900; first gen. offr. commdg. mil. forces of C. of A., 1901-1905.

HYATT, G. O.—Aast. engrnr., Uganda rlyw., Jan., 1908.

HYDE, GEORGE HERBERT MACCARTHY, M.I.C.E., M.I.N.A., M.I.M.E.—B. 1869; apprenticed and asst. man. to H. Bewley, Esq., M.I.C.E., chief engrnr., Colombo Commercial Co., Ceylon; dist. and mech. engrnr., P.W.D., Ceylon, 1900; factory engrnr., with rank and duties of provincial engrnr., 1911; capt., Ceylon artillery volunteers, 1907.

HYSLOP, DR. JAMES, D.S.O.(1901); M.B., C.M. (Edin.).—B. 1856; med. supt., Natal govt. asylum; prin. med. offr., Natal militia, and offr. comdg. Natal medical corps (lieut.-col.); pres. of Natal med. coun.; chrmn. of bd. of health; mem. of pharmacy bd.; mem. of board of trustees of Natal museum; one of Natal's representatives on
council of Cape univ.; formerly ast. physician, Royal Edin., Asyl., Morningside, and of Border Counties Asyl., Melrose; served in S. African war, 1899-1901 (ment. in desps.), and in Natal native rebellion, 1906 (ment. in desps.).

**Hyslop, Sir Thomas, Kt. Bach. (1911), J.P., ex. M.L.A.—B. 1859; educ. Ayr acad.; arrived in Natal, 1882; pres. Natal farmers' confce., 1893-1903; mem. Invasion Losses Enquiry Com., 1899-1903; elected M.L.A. for Umgeni div., 1902; treasr. in Hime ministry, 1903; one of the Natal delega. to Bloemfontein customs confce., 1903; treasr. in Smyth ministry, 1905; attended S. African customs confce., 1906; one of the Natal delega. of S. African National Convention, 1908-09; mem. of rlws. and harb. bd., Union of South Africa.

**Idington, Hon. John, K.C., LL.B. (Univ. of Toronto).—B. 1840; ed. Coll. Inst., Galt, Ontario, and Univ. of Toronto; called to the bar, 1864; Q.C., 1876; judge, exchequer div., high ct. of just. for Ontario, 1904; justice, sup. ct. of Canada, 1905.

**Im Thurn, Sir Everard F., K.C.M.G. (1905), C.B. (1900), C.M.G. (1892), M.A.—B. 1852; ed. at Marlborough and Exeter Coll., Oxon; special mag., Pomeroon Dist., Br. Guiana, 1882 to 1890; gov't. agt., N.W. dists., 1890; agt. cl. clk., C.O., Dec., 1899; col. sec., Ceylon, 1901; admstrd. gov't., Ceylon, 1902; gov't., Fiji, and high comsnr., W. Pacific, 21st June, 1904; retired, 1910; represented Fiji and Western Pacific at the Coronation of H.M. King George V., 1911; editor of the Guiana scientific journal "Timheiri," 1882-7; author of "Among the Indians of Guiana," 1883, and papers on the anthropology, natural history, geography, and history of Guiana; in 1884 made first ascent of Mount Roraima in the interior of Br. Guiana.

**Ingles, F. H.—B. 1873; ed. at U.S. Coll., Westward Ho., Newton Coll., Devon, and Jesus Coll., Cambridge; B.A. Cantab., 1902; asst. dist. comsnr., S. Nigeria, 6th Oct., 1906.

**Ingles, Walter Culpepper Stanser, A.I.C.E.—B. 1868; ed. at Victoria Coll., Jersey; asst. survr., Ceylon, 4th Jan., 1890; dist. survr., 13th Mch., 1897; supt. of application surveys, 1st Jan., 1905; deputy survr.-gen., 15th Oct., 1910.

**Innes, Henry Rose.—B. 1865; ed. at Murraysburg, Cape Colony; practised as attorney in the Transvaal until 1897; served with Nesbit's Horse in S. African war; mem. of Lord Kitchener's cent. bd. for mil. compensation; pres. of special criminal ct., Pretoria, 1902; res. mag., Pretoria, Mch., 1902.

**Innes, Rt. Hon., Sir James Rose, P.C.(1915), K.C.M.G. (1901), K.C.—B. 1855; called to the bar of sup. ct., Cape Colony, 12th Feb., 1878; mem. for Victoria East house of assem., Cape, 1884; subsequently reprtd. Cape div.; atty.-gen., 1st Rhodes' ministry, 17th July, 1890, to May, 1893; selected by Imp. govt. to watch proceedings in connection with trial of reform comtce. prisoners at Pretoria, 1896; atty.-gen. 4th Sprigg ministry, 1900-2; dele. for Cape Colony to attend conf. in Lond. on final ct. of appeal, 1911; ch. just., sup. ct., Transvaal, 29th Mar., 1912; ordinary judge of appeal, sup. ct., Union of S. Africa, 1910.

**Innes, John Ront, barrister-at-law, Lincoln's Inn.—Ed. Edin. and Brussels Unive.; cadet, S. Settlns., Nov., 1886; passed in Malay, 1889; dist. offr., S. Malacca, June, 1890; ditto, N. Malacca, June, 1890; ast. Indian immigrn. agt., Malacca, June, 1889; ag. collr. land rev. and mag., Malacca, June to Nov., 1892; passed final exam. in Dutch, 1893, and in Chinese, 1893; ag. collr. land rev., Singapore, Feb., 1894; acted also as mag., Oct., 1894, to July, 1895; as offl. assignee and regist. of deeds, July to Oct., 1895; ag. astt. col. sec., Oct. to Dec., 1895; ag. collr. land rev. and offr. in charge of treas., also ag. mag. and dep. regist., Malacca, Mar., 1896; collr. of land rev., Penang, May, 1897; ag. sen. dist. offr., prov. Wellesley, Mar., 1898; ag. 1st mag., Penang, Aug., 1898; Apr., 1899; ag. inspr. prisons, S.S., June, 1900; Jan., 1901, and from May to Dec., 1901; census, 1901; deputy public prosecutor, Jan., 1902; sec. to govt., Perak, Feb., 1902; atty.-gen., S.S., Feb., 1906; mem. of committee drafting new cts. and civil procedure act, July, 1906; jud. comsnr., F.M.S., Mar., 1913; chief jud. comsnr., Apr. to Sept., 1913; sat. "Registration of Title in F.M.S."

**Inniss, W. E.—Machinist, survey dept., Leone, Dec., 1866; under gaoler, Freetown, 1871; foreman and machinist, harbour works, 1872; keeper, Freetown gaol, Aug., 1874; asst. of pub. wks., Dec., 1882; served in Yonnie exp., 1887; offr. in charge, Sulymah, 1888.

**Inskipp, Percy Sidney—Clk., admin. off., S. Rhodesia, 1891; ag. sec., 1892; asst. adminstr., 1893; under sec., 1897; joined Lab. staff, B.S.A. Co., 1900; mem. of pioneer exp. (occupation of Mashonaland), 1890; also served with the Mashonaland horse, Matabele reg., 1896 (medal), and Rhodesia field force, 1896 (medal and 2 clasps).

**Ireland, Archibald Edward.—M.R.C. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.P.H. (Oxford); Bart.'s hosp., Lond.; late clinical astt. Birmingham and Midland skin and urinary hospital; med. offr., The Infirmary, B'ham.; dist. med. Hosp., B'ham.; astt. comsnr. and gov't. med. offr., Salt Cay, Turks Is., 1903; gov't. med. and med. offr. of health, Grand Turk, 1904; med. offr. of health, port med. offr., Suvu bacteriologist, Fiji, Apr., 1909.

**Irving, Hon. Sir Wm. Hill K.C.M.G. (1914), LL.D., K.C.—B. 1853; called to the bar, Victoria, 1884; premier of Victoria, 1904-12; H. of R., C. of A., since 1906; atty.-gen. C. A., June, 1913 to Sept. 1914.

**Irving, Charles John, C.M.G. (1881), B. 1831; in col. land and emigrn. office, June, 1859; clk., audit office, 1853; spec. dist. audit office, Mauritius, 1864; auditor-gen., Stellinths., 1867; res. councr., Malacca, 1870; ditto, Penang, 1882; ag. lieut.-gov., Malacca, 1871; and of Penang, 1879; ag. col. sec., 1871, 1875, 1878, and 1883; ret., 1887.

**Irving, Edward A.—Joined Perak F.M.S. service, 25th Mar., 1891; passed final exam. in Malay, Oct., 1891; passed final exam. in Chinese (Hakka dialect), Feb., 1895; ag. collr. land rev., Kinta dist., June, 1895; prot. of Chinese, Lar dist., July, 1896; warden of mines, Selangor, Feb., 1898; warden of mines, Perak, Jan., 1899; passed final exam. in law, July, 1900; inspr. schools, Hong Kong, Apr., 1901; passed in exam. in Cantonese, May, 1905; ag. regist. gen. and M.L.C., July to Sept., 1905; ag. regist. gen. and M.L.C., Sept. to Oct., 1906; ag. regist. gen. and M.L.C., Apr., 1908, to Mar., 1909, and Aug., 1910; passed law exam., 1911; ag. 1st pol. mg., Nov., 1911 to Oct., 1912.

**Irving, Henry Edward.—Ed. at Carey house and Handelslehranstalt, Leipzig; trooper, 9th Lancers, 1899-1902; served in S. Amo...
IRVING, Sir Henry T., G.C.M.G. (1888), C.M.G. (1878), C.M.G. (1874).—B. 1833; clk. to admnstr., O.F.S. Prov., 10th Aug., 1852; clk. to admnstr., O.F.S. Prov., 10th Aug., 1852.

IRVING, Hugh Craufurd.—Asst. dist. commr., Somaliland Prot., June, 1914.

IRVING, Hon. Paulus Emilius, M.A., B.C.L.—B. 1857; ed. Trin. Coll. Sch., Port Hope, and Trin. Coll., Toronto; called to the bar of Ontario, 1880; of B. Columbia, 1882; p. atty. gen., B. Columbia, 1883; judge of the c. of B. Columbia, 1897; spec. commr. in Dist. of Columbia, 1899; judge of the c. of appeal, Columbia, 1909.

IRVING, William Howe.—Apptd. stock prr., Queensland, 1866; junr. offr., customs dept., Brisbane, 1867; 2nd offr., shipping master, etc., Brisbane, 1870; ch. clk., Brisbane, 1883; incl. surv. on amalgamn. of offices, Apr., 1886; clk. of customs and ch. inspr. of distilleries, Queensland, 1893; mem. of imgrn. bd., 1894.

RWIN, Henry Mark, B.A.—B. 1885; ed. Haileybury and Selwyn Coll.; Cambridge exhibitioner; Haileybury exhibitioner; hons. class pos., 1908; asst. res., N. Nigeria, 1908; attached to secretariat, July to Dec., 1911; priv. to ag. gov., C. L. Temple, Esq., C.M.G., 1912.

ISAAC, Charles Powys.—Ck., col. branch, audt. dep., Aug., 1890; clk. in charge of dist., Jan., 1894; detached for service as loc. digtr., Uganda Prot., June, 1895, to Sept., 1897; again as loc. audr., N. Nig., May, 1900, to Aug., 1901; prin. clk., Transvaal aud. off., Apr., 1902; aud. st. aud.-gen., Transvaal, Feb., 1903; aud. to C.C., S. Africa, Oct., 1904; asst. auditor-gen., of S. Africa, 1910.

ISAAC, Francis Whitmore.—3rd asst., Uganda Prot., 8th Dec., 1897; coll., E. Africa rot., 1st Apr., 1902; prov. commr., E.A.P., ug., 1914.

ISAACS, Henry Baber.—B. 1857; clk. of petty sessions and sub-clrk. of taxes, dist. No. 3, Tobago, Jly., 1878; ag. inland rev. offr., Leeward Dist., sc., 1878, to Dec., 1878; ag. 2nd rev. offr., Mar., 1880; 1st rev. offr., May, 1882; rev. offr., and cler. of births and deaths, Carriacou, Nov., 1884; a.J.P.; ag. pol. mag., Carriacou, for 2 months 1887; 1st landing waiter and port offr., St. Vincent, Oct., 1889; pol. mag. and asst. treas., 2nd dist., St. Vincent, July, 1898; pol. mag. and coroner, 2nd dist., St. Vincent, Apr., 1902.

ISAACS, Hon. Isaac Alfred.—B. 1855; called to the bar, Victoria, 1880; Q.C., 1899; L.L.A., Victoria, 1892-1901; solr.-gen., 1893; ty.-gen., 1894-9; and again in 1900; mem. of nat. Fed. Convention, 1897-8; and of first federal parlmt.; atty. gen. in Deakin ministry, 1905-6; judge of High Ct. of Australia, Oct., 1906.

ISAACS, John Owen Rhts.—Ed. Weymouth coll.; 2nd Batt. Hampshire Regt., 1900; S.A.C., 1901-1908; served in S. African war, 1901-2 (queen's medal and five clasps); asst. inspr. of police, Uganda Prot., 11th June, 1909; asst. supt. f police, 1st Apr., 1911.

ISEMONGER, Francis Maxwell.—B. 1876; served under B. N. Borneo Co., June, 1898, to Aug., 1904; asst. collr., Uganda Prot., 9th Sept., 1904; dist. commr., 1909.

ISLINGTON, 1st Baron (cr. 1910), Rt. Hon. Sir John Poynder Dickson-Poynder, 6th Bart., P.C. (1911); G.C.M.G. (1913); K.C.M.G. (1911); D.S.O. (1900); J.P.—B. 1866; ed. at Harrow and Christ Church, Oxford; major and hon. col., Wilts Yeomanry; served in S. Africa, 1900 (Queen's medal, 3 clasps); late lieut., 3rd Royal Scots; mem. L.C.C., 1898-1904; M.P., Chippenham, Wilts, 1892-1910; gov., New Zealand, 1910-1912; chmn. of Indian civ. ser. comn., 1912; parly. under sec. of state for the colonies, 8th Aug., 1914.

ISRAEL, John Wm., I.S.O. (1910).—B. 1850; ent. Tasmanian govt. serv., on transfer of rly. staff to govt., Aug., 1872; was successively rly. audit clk., statn. master, and acctnt. of rly.; transf. to audit off., as chief clk., 1882; subsequently apptd. dep. aud.; aud.-gen. of Tasmania, 1893; transf. to serv. of Com. of Austr., as aud.-gen., 1st Dec., 1901.

IZARD, Rev. Herbert Crawford.—M.A. (Oxon); B. 1869; col. chaplain, Malacca, S. Sttlmts., 19th Oct., 1901; ag. col. chap., Sing., Oct., 1904; confirmed, May, 1905.

IZAT, Norman, M.A. Edin.—B. 1888; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1912; attached to Colombo Kachcheri, Jan., 1913; col. sec.'s office, Apr., 1913; ag. pol. mag., Anuradhapura, June, 1913; ag. office asst., ditto, Nov., 1913; commr. of requests and pol. mag., Pt. Pedro and Chavakachcheri.

JACKMAN, Hon. Edward Michael.—B. 1868; M.H.A. for Placentia and St. Marv's, Newfoundland, 1900; min. of finance and cust., 1900; re-elected to Assembly, 1904.

JACKMAN, Henry Thos.—Crystal Palace engng. schl., 1890-3; pupil and asst. on water and drainage wks. to Messrs. McLandborough and Preston, civ. engrs., 1893-6; in charge of new sewerage wks., Ripon, 1896-7; asst. dist. engrn. on electric tramways, drainage wks., etc., at Sheffield, 1897-1903; exec. engrn. on water and drainage wks., Hong Kong, 1903-1912; ag. san. survr., 1904-1905; seconded for spec. serv. in China, 1908; exec. engrn., 1st grade, 1912.

JACKS, Philip.—Ed. Plymouth Coll.; admtd. solr., sup. ct., England, May, 1900; asst. land offr., Hong Kong, Aug., 1905; J.P., Oct., 1905; commr. for oaths, Oct., 1905; ag. land offr., Apr., 1907, to Apr., 1908; ag. land offr. and offr. recvr. in bankruptcy, Nov., 1908; ag. land offr., Aug. to Nov., 1911; and from 10th Apr., 1913 to 7th Feb., 1914.

JACKSON, Bedver Blaine Lowther.—Ed. Eton and Univ. Coll., Oxford; clk. to atty.-gen., O.R.C., July, 1901; clk. to legis. coun., June, 1902; 1st clk. to atty.-gen., July, 1904; joint editor of law-book, O.R.C., 1906.

JACKSON, Cecil Gower, J.P., F.R.C.I.—B. 1872; ed. private tuition; silver medal, Natal English literature exam., 1891; student interpreter and clk., sec. native affairs off., and clk. in Ikopo and Newcastle magistracies from Nov., 1888; 3rd cls. clk., Newcastle, 1st July, 1892; clk. of ct., Zulu interp., sub-distributor of stamps, and dep. clk. of peace, Impendle, 12th Nov., 1894; clk. of ct., etc., Weenen, 8th July, 1897; 2nd cls. clk., 1st Jan., 1898; frequently acted as mag., Impendle and Weenen, 1895-1901; clk. of ct. and ag. asst. mag., Ladysmith, 1st Jan., 1902; ag. mag., Ladysmith, May-Nov., 1902; ag. asst. mag., Umzinto, Feb., 1903; ag. asst. mag., Newcastle, Aug., 1903; mag. 1st Jan., 1904; 2nd civ. mag., Durban, Jan., 1904, to Nov., 1905; mag., etc.,
Weenen, 11th Nov., 1905; marriage offr., 5th Dec., 1905; mag., Mahlabatini (for spec. purposes), 14th July, 1908; representative native affairs dept. on native educn. advisory bd., Mar., 1909; delimited new magisterial boundaries, and re-adjusted other divisional boundaries, June, 1909; comsnr. to enquire into sentences on native rebels, July, 1909; mag., Ndwandwe (for spec. purposes), 21st Sept., 1909; promoted 2nd div. of mgs., 1st Jan., 1910; judge, native high ct., 19th May, 1910; served in S. African campaign, 1899-1902, and in Natal native rebellion, 1906.

JACKSON, FRANCIS WALTER FITTON.—B. 1881; ed. Dover Coll.; entd. R.A., 1899; served in S. Africa, 1901-2; seconded to W.A.F.F., 30th July, 1904; dist. comsnr., Northern Territories, G. Coast, 1st Jan., 1907; asst. col. sec., G. Coast, 10th March, 1911.

JACKSON, SIR FREDERICK JOHN.—K.C.M.G. (1913); C.B. (1899); C.M.G. (1902); ed. at Shrewsbury Schl. and Jesus Coll., Camb.; 1st cls. asst., Uganda Prot., July, 1894; vice-coms., May, 1895; dep. comsnr., Apr., 1901; dep. comsnr., E. Africa Prot., Apr., 1902; lieut.-gov., 1907; East and Cent. African medal with clasp, Uganda, 1897-98, and Luba and African gen. ser. medal, Uganda, 1900; mem. of exec. and leg. couns., E. Africa Prot., 1907; gov., Uganda Prot., 21st Mch., 1911; assumed govt., 3rd Apr., 1911.

JACKSON, HENRY.—M.H.A., S. Australia, 1906; chmn. of comtees, 1910; speaker of H. of A., 17th Nov., 1911.

JACKSON, COL. HUGH MILBOURNE, R.E.—B. 1858; survey of India, 1883-95; Burmese expdn., 1885-9 (ment. in desps.); ordnance survey of Great Britain, 1895-9; S. African war, 1899-1902; attached to army headqtrs. staff for mapping and reconnaissance; A.A.G. topography, Nov., 1900, to end of war (ment. in desps. and brevet); pres. of Natal-Transvaal boundary, coms., 1902; survr.-gen., Transvaal, Mar., 1903, to May, 1905; attached to intell. dep., S. Africa, June-Nov., 1905; rejd. ordnance surv., Mar., 1906; brevet-col., Apr., 1905; survr.-gen., F.M.S., Aug., 1908.

JACKSON, T.—Curator, botanic station, Antigua, Leeward Is., 1905.

JACKSON, THOS. BEDDARD.—B. 1874; ed. at Bromsgrove coll.; govt. shorthand writer, Trinidad and Tobago, 1st Jan., 1900; ditto, and clk. col. sec.'s office, 8th June, 1901; shorthand writer to asphalt industry coms., 1902; ditto to riot inquiry coms., 1903; sec. to comte. on labour question, 1905-6, ditto to Diego Martin local road bd. coms., 1905-6; ditto to comte. on municipal govt. in Port-of-Spain, 1906; ditto to comte. on extension of local govt., 1906; ditto to coms. on Manzanilla local road bd., 1906; sec. of industrial training bd. of Trinidad and Tobago (in addition to other duties), 1st May, 1907; sec., telephone coms., 1908; sec., plague claims comte., 1908; sec. to Sir Rubert Boyce, 1909; sec., fishing industry comte., 1910; editor of "The Book of Trinidad."

JACKSON, W. B.—Verderer, forest dept., E.A.P., Apr., 1904; senr. asst. conservator of forests, Apr., 1914.

JACKSON, WILFRED EDWARD FRANCIS.—B. 1883; ed. Stonyhurst Coll. and Lincoln Coll., Oxford (classical scholar), B.A. 1905; personal sec. to gov., Trinidad, 1906; priv. sec. to gov. and clk to exec. coun., Bahamas, Sept., 1906, to Oct., 1907; asst. collr., Uganda, Nov., 1907; ag. dist. comsnr., Toro, July, 1911, to Apr., 1912; dist. comsnr., Apl., 1912; ag. asst. chief sec., July-Dec., 1912; 1st asst. sec., Dec., 1912; ag. chief sec., Aug., 1913.

JACKSON, WM. HENBY, C.M.G. (1914); Cadet, Ceylon, 23rd Sept., 1879; pol. mag., May, 1886; asst. govt. agt., 21st June, 1890; collr. of cls., 11th June, 1901; ag. control-rev., in addition to his own duties, July, 1908, Nov., 1908, Jan., 1909, and April, 1910; ret., 1913.

JAFFE, DANIEL, A.M.I.C.E.—Ed. at U. Coll. Schl., London; City and Guilds of L. Cent. Tech. Coll., diploma in civil engineer, 1893-96; articled to Mr. J. Mansergh, P.P. I.C.E., and asst. engr. on B'ham corp. adminstr. water works, 1896-99; asst. eng. B'ham corporation contract waterworks, 1902; asst. engr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1904; exec. engr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, 1906; engineer Hong Kong water supply, Tyne scheme, 1912.

JAMAICA, LORD BISHOP OF, AND ARCHBISHOP OF THE W. INDIES; MOST REV. ESOS NEWTON.—B.D. 1879; D.D. 1880; Hon. D.D. (Oxford) 1897; deacon and priest, Kingston, 1866; consecrated Lord Bishop of Jamaica, 28th Oct., primate of W. Indies, 1893; archbp. of W. Indies, 1897; formerly island curate of St. George's Kingston, Jamaica, 1866-80; bishop in char. dio., Hond., 1881-91; author of "The Church Manual," 1894 (2nd edtn., 1901), "A Book of Special Services" (2nd edtn., 1900), "Catechisms and Devotions for Children and Young People," 1902, "Lectures on the Life of the World to Come," 1904.

JAMES, B.—B. 1874; ed. at Llandover and Merton Coll., Oxford; mathematical master of Merton Coll., 1892-1896; ass't mat. St. Leonard's schl., 1897; second mast., Horsenden schl., 1898; junr. asst. mast., Queen's Coll., Hong Kong, 1898; second mast., King's Coll., Bangkok, 1899; head master, Kowloong, 1902; J.P., 1909; head master, Yasumai, 1910; senr. asst. mast., Queen's Coll., 1912; published a school history of Greece and Egypt.

JAMES, CHARLES CANNIFF, C.M.G. (1896); M.A., F.R.S.C.—B. 1863; ed. pub. ass't schl., Nanapee, Ontario, and Victoria College, Cobourg, Ontario; B.A., 1883; mast., Brock Coll. Inst., 1883 to 1886; prof. of chem., Ontario Agric. Coll., Guelph, 1886 to 1891; min. of agric. for Ontario and sec., sugar industries, 1891; coms. of Dominica to investigate agricultural conditions of Canada.

JAMES, C. D.—Apptd. after comp't exam. clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv., and assigned to the C.O., Dec., 1907.

JAMES, FREDERICK SETON, C.M.G. (1896); B. 8th Apr., 1870; ed. at Charterhouse abroad; asst. dist. coms., Niger Cast., 1896; in charge at Opobo and Akwete, 1897; with peaceful mission to Bende in 1897; dist. coms., 1897; serv. as polit. offr. in expdn. at Ekuris, Cross River, 1898; settled dispute Qua country after cent. div. expdn., 1899; thanks of S. of S.; divsnl. coms., 1901; int'l. polit. offr. with Aro field force, 1901 (medal); rec'd. thanks of dir.-gen. of int'l. S. of S. in connection with map of Arooperan ag. sec. and dep. high coms., 1903; with Katsina patrol, Nov., 1905 (clasp); prov. coms., and int'l. of exec. and legis. couns. of S. Nigeria on admin. formation, 1906; ag. col. sec. from 29th Mar., 1907; dep. gov., Apr. and Sept., 1907; ag. col. sec., deputy gov. on various occasions from 1908.
JARDINE, Douglas James.—Ed. at Westminster and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; 2nd cls. classical trip, June, 1910; B.A., 1910; M.A., 1914; clk., chief sec.'s off., Cyprus, Nov., 1910; ag. priv. sec. to O.A.G. and clk. of exec. council, July to Oct., 1911; ag. asst. sec. (now ch. asst. sec.) to gov't. from May to Oct., 1912, and from June to Nov., 1913; jun. asst. sec., Dec., 1912; passed in modern Greek, June, 1912; joint-editor "Handbook of Cyprus," 1913.

JARRETT, Michael Lewis, M.R.C.S. (Lond.), L.R.C.P. (Edin.).—Asst. col. surg. Sherbro, W. Africa, 1882; is a J.P.

JARVIS, Lieut.-Col. Arthur Leonard Fitzgerald, I.S.O. (1905).—B. 1852; entd. Canadian govt. service, 1868; priv. sec. to P.M.G., 1882 to 1885; and to min. of agric., 1885 to 1892; sec. of dept. of agric., 1896; commanded Gov.-General's Foot Guards, 1899 to 1904; asst. deputy min. of agric., 1909.

JARVIS, Bertie Hill.—Ck., Wallings water wks., Antigua, 1900; overseer of roads, dists. 1 and 2, 1902; overseer of roads and offr. in charge of Wallings water wks., 1903; J.P., 1910; offl. M.L.C., 1909-1910, 1910-1912, 1913-1914; ag. supt. of telephones, 1911; chmn., St. John's City comnrs., 1913; ag. col. engrnr., June, 1906 to Jan., 1907, and from Mar., 1909 to Mar., 1910; ag. surv. of pub. wks., June, 1910 to Oct., 1911, Nov., 1911 to July, 1912, and from Jan., 1913 to Sept., 1914.

JARVIS, Edward Blackwell.—B. 1873; 2nd clk., col. sec.'s office, Leeward Is., 1890; clk. of gov.'s office, 1891; ag. 1st clk., 1891; 1st clk. col. sec.'s office, Mar. to June, 1896. On reorganisation of office, apptd. 2nd clk.; ag. ch. clk., and clk. to fed., exec., and legis. couns. and local legis. coun. of Antigua, Apr., 1897, to Jan., 1898, and July to Dec., 1899; P.S. to ag. gov., June to Oct., 1899; ch. clk. col. sec.'s off., and clk. to fed., exec., and legis. couns. and local legis. coun., Antigua, 3rd July, 1901; dir., pub. offr.'s guarantee fund 6th Dec., 1902; asst. col. sec., Leeward Is., Feb., 1903; ag. col. sec., Leeward Is. and Island sec., Antigua, 24th Mch. to 15th Oct., 1905; ag. fed. treasur., Aug. to Oct., 1905; trade and income tax assessor, 27th Dec., 1905; ag. col. sec., Leeward Islds. and Island sec., Antigua, on several occasions in 1907, 1908, 1909, 1911 and 1912; J.P., Antigua, 1908; chmn., St. John's City comnrs., 1st Jan., 1910 to 10th Feb., 1911; pres. of Antigua defence res. corps, 30th Sept., 1911, to 12th May, 1912; asst. chief sec. and registr-gen. of births, deaths and marriages, Uganda, 15th July, 1912; ag. chief sec., Uganda, 24th July to 29th Dec., 1912, 5th to 22nd June, 1913, and from 8th July, 1913.

JARVIS, Ernest Frederick.—B. 1862; ent. civ. ser., Canada, as 3rd cls. clk. in post office dept., 1881; priv. sec. to the S. of S. and subsequently to the min. of militia and defence, 1892-1895; transf'd. to dept. of militia and defence, 1893; chief clk., 1903; sec. to militia coun., 1903, and asst. deputy min., 1909.

JARVIS, T. Leslie H.—Dep. regir. of marriages, births and deaths, 1890-2, and census offr. for parish of St. George, Antigua, 1891; clk. and priv. sec. to admstrs. and clk. to exec. coun. from 1895; ag. clk. to bd. of health, Dominica, 1896; priv. sec. to ag. gov., Leeward Is., Sept., 1904; ag. treasur., mem. of exec. and legis. couns. and of quarantine bd., comnrs. of piers, recvr. of wrecks and regir. of shipping, Dominica, Aug., 1905 to Apr., 1906; and on two other occasions for short periods in 1906 and 1909; comnrs.,
Virgin Is., mem. of gen. legis. coun., Leeward Is., Aug., 1909; mem. exec. coun., Leeward Is., Jan., 1910; ag. comsnr., Montserrat, 3rd May, 1913 to 1st Jan., 1914.

JEBB, R. H.—Asst. local auditor, E.A.P., 1909.

JEBB, R. R.—B.A. (Oxon); B. 1882; asst. auditor, S. Leone, Jan., 1907; asst. auditor, E.A.P., Nov., 1909.

JEFFERY, GEORGE, F.S.A.—Scholarship, R. Coll. of Art and Science, 1872; scholarship in architecture, R. Academy of London (1874); F.R.I.B.A., 1892; architect to Rt. Rev. Bishop in Jerusalem and the East, 1892; hon. corres. mem. of Imperial Institute of Archaeology of Russia, 1897; local sec. for Cyprus Society of Antiquaries; inspr. of pub. wks., Cyprus, 1898; curator of ancient monuments, Cyprus, 1903; author of "Summary of Architectural Monuments of Cyprus," and of several papers on the mediaeval archaeology of Cyprus and Jerusalem.

JEFFRIES, CHARLES WILLIAM.—B. 1882; Computer, Royal Observatory, Greenwich, 1897; computer, Royal Observatory, Cape Colony, 1902; 1st asst., Hong Kong Observatory, 1907; chief asst., ditto, June, 1912.

JEKYLL, Lieut.-Col. Sir Herbert, K.C.M.G. (1901), R.E., C.M.G. (1885).—B. 1846; lieut. R.E., Apr., 1866; employed under War Office and Trinity House in 1868 to 1870, and destruction of sunken ships, from submarine mining, and under G.P.O. in the telegraph dept., from 1870 to 1873, and 1874 to 1876; served in the campaign of 1873-74 on the G. Coast; priv. sec. to the Earl of Carnarvon, Jan., 1877, to Feb., 1878; sec. to the col. defence comttee, 1878; sec. to the rov. coman. on the defence of Br. possessions and commerce abroad, 1879-82; specially employed to visit and report on the defences of Singapore and Colombo, 1883-4; sec. col. defence comttee, 1885; priv. sec. to Lord Carnarvon, viceroy of Ireland, June, 1885, to Jan., 1886; sec. to rov. coman. for Melbourne centennial exhib., 1888; priv. sec. to lord-lieut. of Ireland, 1892-5; sec. to the rov. coman. for the Paris exhibition, 1900.

JELF, ARTHUR SELBORNE.—B. 1876; ed. Marlborough and Exeter Coll., Oxford (exhr.); 2nd cls. class. mods., 1897; 3rd cls. lit. hum., 1899; B.A., 1899; cadet, F.M.S. civ. serv., 1899; ag. asst. sec. to res., Selangor, Jan., 1901; passed final exam. in Malay, May, 1901; ag. dist. offr., Kuala Langat, Selangor, Dec., 1903; asst. sec. to res., Selangor, Jan., 1905; ag. sec. to res., Negri Sembilan, March, 1905; ag. dist. offr., Pekan, Pahang, March, 1907; ag. asst. sec. to res., Perak, Oct., 1908; asst. general adviser to Johore govt. Jan., 1911.

JENKINS, THE HON. JOHN GREELEY.—B. 1851; mem. H. of A., S. Aust., 1887 to 1905; min. of ed. and N. territory, 1891-2; comsnr. of pub. wks., 1892; ditto, 1894-9; chief sec., 1899-1901; premier and ch. sec., 1901-5; agent-gen. in London, July, 1905, to July, 1908.

JENKS, STUART DIXON, LL.B., K.C.—B. 1869; ed. Pioton Acad., Dalhousie Univ., and Cornell Univ.; called to the bar, 1896; practised law in Amherst, Nova Scotia, 1896-1908; K.C., 1908; dep. atty.-gen., Nova Scotia, 1908.

JERSEY (7th EARL OF), VICTOR ALBERT GEORGE CHILD WILLENS, P.C., G.C.B. (1900), G.C.M.G. (1890).—B. 1845; lord-lieut. co. Oxford; was lord in waiting to H.M. Queen Victoria; gov., N.S. Wales, 1890-3; represented H.M.'s govt. at coll. confee., Ottawa, 1894.

JETTÉ, SIR LOUIS AMABLE, K.C.M.G., LL.D.—B. 1836, at L'Assomption, Quebec, and ed. ther called to the bar, 1857; el. to H. of C., 1871; judge of the super. ct., Quebec, 1878; prof. of civil law, Laval Univ., LL.D., 1878; comm. for revision of civil code, 1887; lieut. gov., Quebec, 1898-1908; mem. Alaskan Boundary Tribunal, 1903; chief just. Court of King Bench for the Prov. of Quebec, 1909; ret. 1911.

JEWELL, M.—B. 1880; Apptd., after comp. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., assigned to the C.O., Apr., 1899, conf. clk. 1911.

JEWELL, NORMAN PARSONS.—M.D.; B.C.; B.A.O., Trin. Coll., Dub.; L.M., Rotunda, D.C.; B.A. (Moderator), Trin. Coll., Dub.; late anesthetist, Dun's Hosp., Dub.; asst. med. of Seychelles, 1910; J.P.; and chmn. local bldg. health, Praslin and La Digue; med. supx. leper asylum.

JOHN, WM. AUGUSTUS.—Ed. at Wesleyan schl., Lagos; passed civ. ser. exam., 1902; 1st cls. certif., Lond. Coll. Preceptors, 1903; sec. secretariat, Lagos, Sept., 1903; transf'd. to judg. dept., Apr., 1904; 6th cls. clk., Feb., 1905; cls. clk., Apr., 1906; 2nd cls. clk., aud. July, 1907.

JOHNS, FRED, F.J.L.—B. 1868; ed. Cornw. England; on Adelaide newspaper literary sect. from 1885 to 1914; leader of the first Hansard staff, S. Australian parlmt. since Jan., 1914; author of "John's Notable Australian" (1894 and 1896), and of "Fred John's Anna" (mainly a biographical record of Australian prominent people).

JOHNS, HAROLD THOMAS SMEDLEY.—B. 1880; asst. mast., grammar schl., Dominica, Sept., 1904; ag. head master, April to Sept., 1905; ag. head master and sub-inspr. of schoo Feb. to Sept., 1909; govt. offr., trs., Dominica, Nov., 1910.

JOHNSON, D. O.—B. 1873; entd. Bahamas civ. ser., 1904; Out Island comsnr. (3rd div.), 1909; 2nd div., 1910; 1st div., 1914.

JOHNSON, E. O. I.S.O. (1911).—Ed. Enon Coll. and Harr. Coll., Barbados; 2nd treas. offr., Montserrat, 1884; 1st treas. offr., 1st clk. treas., St. Kitts-Nevis, 1891; 1st treas. offr., 1894; ag. treas., Dec., 1896, to Sept., 1897; asst. treas., S. Leone, Nov., 1897; clk. treas., Mar., 1899; has acted as col. sec.

JOHNSON, F. E. G.—B.A., Cantab; asst. dist. comsnr., So. Nigeria, Apr., 1900; dist. comsnr., July, 1902; asst. sec. (temporarily), Feb. to Aug., 1904; ag. pol. mag., Calabar, Aug., 1904.

JOHNSON, GEORGE CUNYNGHAM.—B. 1875; 2nd clk., treas., St. Kitts, Apr., 1894; ag. extra. rev. offr., May, 1895; 2nd clk. admstr.'s office, cd. of legis. coun., Mar., 1896; ag. acctnt. treas. Jan., 1897; audit clk. and clk. legis. coun., St. Kitts-Nevis, May, 1897; clk. to admstr., exec., and legis. couns., and clk. to bd. of health, Jan., 1901; asst. priv. sec. (unpaid) to H.E. Chas. T. JOHNSON, GEORGE WILLIAM, C.M.G. (1904).—M.A.—B. 1857; scholar of Trin. Coll., Camb.
ranger and 3rd class classics, 1880; apptd., after compet. exam., to be a clk. in the office of the co. of state for the cols., Mar., 1881; sec. to eastern currency comte., 1893; asst. priv. sec. hr. Chamberlain, May, 1896; priv. sec. to Sir Meade, Sept., 1896; 1st class clk., Mar., 1897; in clk., 30th June, 1900; mem. of S.S. currency mte., 1902-3; mem. of inter-departmental mte. on cable-landing rights; joint sec. to np. Conf., 1907.

JOHNSON, HENRY STAFFORD BROWLOW.—1876; cadet, Sarawak, 1897; asst. resid., 1901; id cls. res. in charge of Upper Rejang, 1903.

JOHNSON, JOHN TAYLOR CONNELL.—F.R.C.S. (Ed.), D.T.M. and H. (Camb.), 1905; Fellow society of trop. med.; fellow of Royal Inst. Pub. Health; mem. B.M.A.; b. 1867; asst. hl. surg., G. JOHNSON, HON. W. D. M.H.A.—Min. of ib. wks., W. Australia, 1911.

JOHNSTON, ALEXANDER.—B. 1867; ed. at ib. schls., and St. Francis Xavier Coll., Antimish, Nova Scotia; entd. local legis. of Nova Scotia, April, 1897, as repres. for Cape Breton Co., Nova Scotia; resig. in 1900 and entd. fed. parlmt., same year and sat continuously until 1908; min. marine and fisheries of Canada, June, 1908.

JOHNSTON, HARRY FREDERICK.—B. 1853; contract survr., W. Australia, Jan., 1874; ag. aff. survr., Nov., 1883; confirmed, Feb., 1885; surveyed and triangulated Kimberley dist., and discovered Elvire and Mary rivers, where goldfields have been found; in charge of constr. telegraph, Roebourne to Derby, 1886-9; survr.-en., July, 1896.

JOHNSTON, R. FLEMING.—B. 1874; M.A., Magdalen Coll., Oxford (1901); Gray prizeman, Edin. Univ., 1894; prox. acc. Lord Rector's essay; st. cl. certa. Eng. lit., mod. history and constitutional law, Edin.; exhibitioner, Magdalen Coll., 1894; mentioned hon. causa Stanhope essay, 1898; B.A. (hons.), 1898; cadet, Hong Kong, 1898; ag. elk. of councils, 1899; priv. sec. to H.E. the administrator; ag. asst. col. sec., 1900; priv. sec. to the governor, 1900-1901; passed in Chinese, Oct., 1901; ag. asst. col. sec. and elk. of councils, 1901-1904; ag. sec. to gov't., Veihaiwei, 1904; dist. offr. and mag., ditto, 1906.

JOHNSTON, ROBERT MACKENZIE, I.S.O.(1903), S.S.(1879).—Regisr.-gen. and gov't. statistician of Tasmania; ed. Andersonian Univ., Glasgow; apptd. to organise and superintend the working of the acttn.'s and traffic audit branch of the first rly. opened in Tasmania (1870); transfed. to service of asmanian Govt. (1872); ch. clk. in auditor-gen.'s office (1880); apptd. to reorganise and conduct the then combined offices of regisr.-gen. and gov't. statistician (1882); roy. commr. to inquire and report on the fisheries of the col. of Tasmania (1882); apptd. salmon fisheriee commr. (1888-90); chmn. of boundaries bd. of advice (1890); author of "Systematic Account of the Geology of Tasmania," and other scientific wks.; fellow of the Roy. Statis. Soc. of Lond.; mem. of the coun. of the Roy. Soc. of Tasmania and of the Australasian Assoc. for Advancement of Science; fellow of the Roy. Geog. Soc. of Australasia.

JOHNSTONE, BANNER CARRUTHERS.—B. 1882; ed. Eton and Trin. Coll., Camb.; B.A. (Cantab.); passed R.G.S. survey course, 1908; asst. supt. of surveys, Ceylon, 21st Oct., 1909; asst. collr. (now asst. dist. commr.) 23rd Apr., 1913.

JOHNSTONE, CHARLES EDWARD.—Ed. Cheltenham and Westward Ho colleges; lieut., 4th Batt. P.A. Somerset L.I., 1885-1887; asst. supt. of pol., Madras presidency, 1887-88; served in 1st Batt. Durham L.I. JOHNSTONE, ROBERT, I.S.O. (1912)—Temporary clk., audit office, Jamaica, 1878; 3rd class clk., col. sec.'s office, 1879; sec. to bd. of supervision, poor relief, Sept., 1886; 1st cls. clk., col. sec.'s off., Jan., 1902; senr. clk., Jan., 1905; ag. asst. col. sec., 1905 and 1906; asst. col. sec., Dec., 1906; ag. col. sec., May, 1907, six mons. in 1908, three mons. in 1909, five mons. in 1910, five mons. in 1911, and seven mons. in 1912; was also sec. schools commn. from 1883 to 1902; and asst. gov't. meteorologist from 1880 to 1899; sec. to commrs. to inquire into customs defalcations, 1889; conduct of two public offrs., 1890; Milk River baths, 1892; ed. in Jamaica, 1898; mem. and man. dir. of local bd. of Mans. Titchfield (school) trust property, 1899 to 1902; apptd. to be one of three hurricane loan officers, in 1903.

JOHNSTONE, SIR ROBERT STEWART, Kt. Bach. (1915).—Ed. at Trin. Coll., Dublin; B.A. (honors and medal in history and political science), 1882; LL.B., 1894; M.A., 1895; Holt scholar, Gray's Inn, 1885; called to the Irish bar 1886; called to the bar at Gray's Inn, Jan., 1889; lieut., 3rd (Militia) Batt. JONES, CHARLES BENJAMIN.—B. 1882; 6th cls. clk., treasy dept., S. Nigeria, 1909; 5th cls. clk., 1906; 4th cls. clk., div. commr.'s off., Bonny, 1906; prov. commr.'s off., E. Prov., 1906; 2nd cls. clk., Jan., 1907; head clk., sol.-gen.'s off., E. Prov., Sept., 1909; 1st cls. clk., Jan., 1912.

JONES, CHARLES HARRISON.—B. 1884; ed. Reading and St. John's Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1907; pol. mag., Puttalam, Jan., 1909; asst. gov't. agt., Colombo and Negombo dists., July, 1910; ag. asst. gov't. agt., Hambantota, Apr., 1912; pol. mag., Matara, May, 1912; ag. asst. gov. agt., Mannar, Feb., 1913.

JONES, CHARLES JEROME, C.M.G. (1914), I.S.O., B.A.—B. 1847; ent. civ. serv., Canada, 1875; apptd. ch. clk., 1883; asst. gov't.-gen.'s sec., 1909; retired, 1914.

JONES, EDWARD RUTTER.—Acted aidwaiter, customs, Antigua, 1875 to 1880; apptd. cashier, treasy., Antigua, Oct., 1880; landing waiter, customs, Antigua, 1881; acted 1st clk., audit off., Leeward Is., 1887 and 1892; apptd. 1st indoor offr., treasy., Antigua, 1895; ag. treas., Antigua, Sept., 1899, Oct., 1900, July, 1901, May, 1902, and Mar.
JONES, G. A.—B. 1889; appt., after compet. exam., clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. ser., and assigned to the C.O., Dec., 1907.

Griffith prize, 1906-8; holder of certif. in forestry; ag. agric. and science master, Antigua grm. schl., 1909; asst. curator, botanic gardens, Dominica, Aug., 1909; in charge of agric. schl., Dominica, Aug., 1909, to Jan., 1910; ag. asst. sec. to permanent exhibtn. comtee., 1909.

JONES, HOWEL, K.C., B.A. (Oxon. and Cape).—Barr.-at-law; ed. S. African Coll., Cape Town, Pembroke Coll., Oxford, and Mid. Temp.; asst. law adviser, atty.-gen.'s off., Cape Town, Mar., 1904; solr.-gen., Grahamstown, 1st July, 1911.

JONES, JOSEPH.—Trained at Kew Gardens; curator, botanic gardens, Dominica, 1892; sec. to permanent exhibtn. comtee.; sec. to agric. experiments comtee.

JONES, LLEWELLYN A. F.—Asst. dist. commnr., E.A.P., 18th Dec., 1908; junr. asst. sec., Feb., 1912.

JONES, OWEN KIRKPATRIC.—B. 1886; ed. Winchester Coll., and Hertford Coll., Oxford; M.A., 1908; asst. dist. commnr., G. Coast, 29th Apr., 1914.

JONES, PATRICK N. H., M.I.C.E.—Ed. King's Coll., Lond., applied sciences; pupil and asst., Edward Easton & Co., C.E., 1883-1889; res. engrnr., Barbados Water Supply Co., 1889 to 1895; ag. D.P.W., Barbados, Sept. to Oct., 1894; thanked by legis. coun. for services in drafting waterworks bill, 1894; apptd. engrnr. in charge of waterworks surveys, Trinidad, 1895; ag. res. engrnr. of water and sewerage works, Feb. to Nov., 1898; and Jan. to Oct., 1900; in charge of construction of water and sewerage works, 1900 to 1903; mem. of comtee. on tech. educn. in the colony, 1902; asst. D.P.W., Hong Kong, 3rd April, 1903; ag. D.P.W. and mem. of exec. and legis. couns., 1904-5, and 1909; dir. of pub. wks., Gold Coast, 1910.

JONES, S. T.—Ed. Wes. high schl., S. Leone; spec. prize for "marked proficiency" in studies, 1895; R. coll. of preceptors and Pitman's shorthand certificates; appointed 6th cls. clk., P.O., Niger Coast Prot., 1898; 3rd cls. clk., high commnr.'s off., 1900; 2nd cls. clk., 1902; Aro medal and clasp, 1902; 1st cls. clk., secretariat, 1903; sen. clk., secretariat, S. Nigeria, 1904, chief clk., ditto, 1905.

JONES, SIR WM. HENRY HYNDMAN, KT., BACH. (1906).—Barrister-at-law, Lincoln's Inn; LL.B., Cantab.; b. 1847; ag. sen. pol. mag., Barbados, 1880; commnr. to inquire into working of pol. force, 1880; ag. judge of assct. ct. of appeal, Jan., 1881; imag., 1st dist., St. Lucia, Mar., 1881; M.L.C., ditto, Oct., 1881; deleg. to W. Indian telegraph confce., May, 1882; ag. ch. just., St. Lucia and Tobago, Jan., 1883; ag. atty.-gen., and mem. of exec. coun., Feb., 1883; ag. ch. just. of St. Lucia and Tobago; mem. of Windwards ct. of appeal, Sept., 1886; mag., and mem. of exec. and legis. couns., Grenada, Mar., 1887; res. mag. for different districts of Jamaica, April, 1888, to Feb., 1893; ag. puisne judge, Jamaica, May, 1893, to June, 1895; ag. atty.-gen., June, 1895; super-numerary res. mag., Jamaica, May, 1896; puisne judge, S. Sttlmts., 3rd Dec., 1896; ag. jus. oomsmnr., in addition to other duties, 25th Mr., 1903, to 3rd Feb., 1904; jud. oomsmnr., 16th Jan., 1904; ch. jud. oomsmnr., 1st Jan., 1906; ch. jus. S. Sttlmts., 22nd Aug., 1906; ret., July, 1914.

JONES, SIR W. H. QUAYLE, KT. BACH. (1882-83); temporary puisne judge, G. Coast (1882 and 1883); mem. of Lond. exec. and clk. of local comtee. for the Col. and Indian Exhib., 1886; Queen's advoc., 1883; ch. just., W. Afr. Sttlmts., 1887; ret., 1895; chmnr. of sessions.

JONES, W. PATRICK.—Impl. service, 1892; clk., treas., Transvaal, 18th Mar., 1892; priv. sec. to col. treas., Apr., 1903; principal clk. treas., 1st July, 1904; principal clk., dept. finance, U. of S. Africa, 1910; chief clk., treas. Union of S. Africa, 1st Aug., 1912.

JORDAN, GIBBS CLAUDE BOBLAKE.—Entd. dept. of just., New Zealand, 1883; clk., 1900; under sec. for just. and prac., 1912.

JORDAN, GREGORY PAUL.—M.R. and Edin. (Edin.), 1880; M.R.C.S. (Eng.), 1884; Med.; F.R.I. Pub. Health; late ass't. dept., Edin. Royal Infirmary; ass't. to lect. diseases of the eye, Edin. Univ.; late Maternity hosp., Edin.; house surg., Dace's county hosp., 1883; ag. res. accoucheur, Thomas's hosp., Lond., 1884; late clk. in hosp. for women, Soho Square, 1902; ag. col. Hosp. Hong Kong, 1886; J.P.; health offr. of the Hosp. Hong Kong, 1888; pro-Chancellor, Univ. of Hong Kong; lecturer on trop. med., Univ. of Hong Kong, and mem. of the ct. and coun. of the consulting surg., Alice Memorial and Netter's hosps.

JORGENSEN, C. R. E.—Capt. 4th Batt. Irish Regt.; ed. at Uppingham; served in Africa, 1900-1901 (two medals with five clasps); asst. polit. offr., Somaliland, Sept., 1905.

JOSCELNYE, R. H.—B. 1852; transferred from Royal Niger Company's service to supplementary clerk, Jan., 1900.

JOSEPH, GERARD ABRAHAM.—B. 1870; sec. to Mr. Just, Clarence, 1891; in charge of Colombo museum, during director's absence, 24th Mar. to 29th Apr., 1892; librarian, Colombo museum, 22nd Oct., 1893; ag. 3rd ast., P.M., 1st to 15th Sept., 1898; ag. director, Colombo museum, 2nd to 10th July, 1900; in charge of Colombo museum, 1st Mar. to 3rd Apr., 1901; in charge of Colombo museum, 30th Mar., 1901; ag. director, Colombo museum, 30th June, 1901, to 13th Feb., 1907; acted as librarian of museum on two occasions prior to being confirmed; hon. sec. of Ceylon branch of Royal Asiatic Soc., since 1893; also hon. treas. since 1907; ed. Class V. of the civil serv., Jan., 1913.

JULL, MARTIN EDWARD.—Ed. Brighton Gratz. schl.; articled 3 yrs. and afterwards asst. clk. with a firm of survrs. of city of London; ed. P.W.D., W. Australia, Jan., 1878; ch. clk., 1892; under sec. P.W., July, 1895; pub. sec. oomsmnr., Apr., 1905.

JUST, ALBERT WOLFGANG, B.A. (1891).—Officer, State of Perak, July, 1892; passed exam. in Malay, Aug., 1893; ag. ch. just. mag. and collr. of land rev., Krian, Jul., 1894; ag., Seremban, Jan., 1903.

JUST, SIR HARTMANN WOLFGANG, K.C.M.G. (1911), C.B. (1902), C.M.G. (1900), B.A. (1877).—B. 1854; appointed, after course exam., clk. in office of sec. of state for col., 3rd June, 1878; ed. at Corpus Christi...
OXFORD; was an open scholar on the foundation; 1st class in classical mods., 1874; Taylorian exhibitor; pioneer for German, 1876; 2nd class in final classical school, 1877; asst. priv. sec. to the late Earl of Derby, 6th Feb., 1883, to Col. F. A. Stanley (now Earl of Derby), 24th June, 1885, and Mr. Stanhope, 3rd Aug., 1886; priv. sec. to Mr. Osborne Morgan, 6th Feb. to 3rd Aug., 1886; asst. priv. sec. to Sir H. Holland (now Lord Knutsford), 12th Jan., 1887, and to the Marquess of Ripon, 17th Aug., 1892; asst. sec. to the col. confce., 1887; 1st class clk., Apr., 1895; priv. clk., Mar., 1897; accompanied Rt. Hon. Joseph Chamberlain on his visit to S. Africa, 1902-3; asst. under-sec. of state, Jan., 1907; jt. sec. to Imp. Confce., 1907; sec. to Imp. Confce. in naval and mil. defence, 1909; visited Canada, 1910; also Australia and New Zealand, 1914; permanent sec. to Imp. Confce.; registr. of the Order of St. Michael and St. George; represents O. on advisory comitee. of commil. intell., B. f T.

KAINE, Hon. John Charles.—B. 1854; ed. commil. Acad., Quebec; elec. mem. of exec. coun. or Quebec West, 1904; re-elec., 1908 and 1912; min. without portfolio, 8th Jan., 1906.

KANTHACK, Francis Edgar, M.I.C.E., L.I.M.E.—J.P. for all Provs., U. of S. Africa; graduated at the Associate of Roy. Indian engrng. Ill., Cooper's Hill, 1890-94; apptd. to Indian ub. wks. dept., Oct., 1894; served as asst. and exec. engrnr., Punjab irrigtn. branch, P.W.D., 1895 to Oct., 1906; apptd. (under agreement) dir. of irrigtn., Cape Colony, Oct., 1906, and "director" in terms of sec. 3 (1) of Act No. 32 of 1906, to advise and assist the comsrr. of pub. wks. in matters relating to irrigtn.; resigned, Indian serv. and joined Cape civ. serv., Oct., 1908; is a mem. of the geological coman.; apptd. director of irrigtn. for the U. of S. Africa and "director" in terms of sec. 3 (1) of Act 32 of 1906 (Cape), and ch. engrnr. irrigtn. in terms of ec. 5 (1) of Act 27 of 1908 (Transvaal), with effect rom 26th Sept., 1910.

KARLSON, A., M.I.C.E.—Chief engrnr., survey Selati Rlwy., 1892-96; ditto, Pietersburg Rlwy., 1896-99; manager, Pretoria Waterworks, 1898-1903; town engrnr., Pretoria, 1899-1902; consulting engrnr., Pretoria municipality, 1902-904; hydro. survr., irrigation dept., Transvaal, 26th July, 1904.

KAY, Albert Sidney.—B. 1885; ed. Uppingham schl. and Wadham coll., Oxford; classical mods., cls. I.; lit. hum., cls. III.; B.A. 1908; set. res., N. Nigeria, 7th Nov., 1908.

KEAN, Hon. Abraham.—M.H.A., Bonavista, Newfoundland, 1885-89, Bay de Verde, 1897; mem. exec. coun. (without portfolio), 1897; ag. min. agricul. and mines, 1898.

KEATING, Hon. John Henry.—B. 1872; called to the bar, Tasmania, 1894; senator for Tasmania, C. of Aust., 1901; min. without portfolio, 5th July, 1905; vice-pres. of exec. coun., 3rd Oct., 1906; min. for home aff airs, Jan., 1907.

KEAY, David Doig.—Clk., Natal govt. rly., 1901-2; clk., law dept., Transvaal, Mar., 1902; ch. clk., adminstr. branch, atty-gen.'s off., Nov., 1903; ch. clk., July, 1904; ag. under-sec. or just., U. of S. Africa, May, 1911; chief clk., lept. of just., 1st Apr., 1912.

KEEFER, Thomas Coltrin, C.M.G. (1878), C.E.—B. 1821; engrnr. of several rlyws. and other wks. in Canada; was exec. comanr. for the Dominion of Canada at the Paris Exhibn., 1878.

KEITH, Robert Donald.—M.A., M.D., Aberdeen; physiologist, etc., S. Sttlmts., Mar., 1906; ag. govt. pathologist, Aug., 1906, to Mar., 1907; principal, med. schl., Feb., 1909.

KELLY, C. C.—Supernum. marshal, Esseguibo, Dec., 1873; ag. clk., Suddie treasy., Oct., 1883; ordinary marshal, provost marshal's office, Georgetown, June, 1884; mag.'s clk., Esseguibo, Aug., 1887; ag. ch. clk., pol. mag.'s office, Georgetown, June, 1893.

KELLY, F. L.—Asst. conservator of forests, E.A.P., Jan., 1913.

KELLY, Sir Henry Greene, Kt. Bach. (1906).—Ed. Trin. Coll., Dub.; honorman and prizeman in hist. and political science; B.A. and LL.B.; called to the bar, King's Inn, Dub., Mich. Term, 1884; apptd. a puisne judge in the Niger Territories, 1891; acted on several occasions as chief justice; chief justice, 1899; chief justice of Southern Nigeria, 1900; ret., 10th Feb., 1908.

KELLY, Hon. Hugh Thomas.—B. 1858; ed. St. Michael's Coll., Toronto, and Toronto Univ.; called to the bar, 1886; K.C., 1908; pres., York Co. Law Assoc., 1910 and 1911; chmn., Toronto pub. lib. bd, for 3 years; a gov. of Toronto Univ., 1906-1912; judge of high ct. of Ontario, 1911.

KELLY, Percy James.—B. 1876; M.B., Ch.B., Glasgow, 1906; house surg., W. Kent general hosp., Maidstone, 1907-8; employed by govt. of Bengal on famine duty, 1907; certif. Lond. schl. of trop. med., 1908; apptd. to W. African med. serv., G. Coast, 1908; med. offr., Hong Kong, 1910; med. offr. to Victoria gaol and visiting med. offr. to Tung Wa hospital; med. offr. in charge of infectious diseases hosp., Kennedy Town; registr., med. coll., Ceylon, 1912.

KELSICK, Oscar Richardson.—Ag. cashier, savings bank, Antigua, 21st Aug., 1906; apptd. as ditto, 16th Jan., 1908; ag. acctnt., savings bank, 16th Jan., 1908; apptd. as ditto, 1st Sept., 1908; ag. acctnt., treasy., 1st May to 4th Aug., 1909; junr. audit clk., 12th June, 1909; ag. gov. offr. (acctnt.), treasy., Dominica, 16th Apr. to 31st Aug., 1910.

KELSON, Jacob Walter.—Clk., survr.'s dept., G. Coast, 1885; ch. warder and med. dresser, lun. asyl., Accra, 1887.

KEMP, Hon. Albert Edward.—B. 1858; ed. Public Schl., Clarenceville, Quebec and Lacolle Acad.; pres. of Canadian Manufacturers' Assocn., 1895 and 1896; pres. of board of trade of the City of Toronto 1899 and 1900; elec. to H. of C., Canada, 1900; re-elec., 1904 and 1911; mem. of the Privy Council for Canada and min. without portfolio in Mr. Borden's cabinet, Oct., 1911.

KEMP, Joseph Horsford.—B. 1874; B.A., Cape Univ.; barrister-at-law, Lincoln's Inn; cadet, Hong Kong, 1898; land offr., New Territory, 1899; registr., land court, May, 1900; ag. 2nd pol. mag., 1900 to 1904; ag. 1st pol. mag., Sept.-Oct., 1904; asst. sec., sanitary bd., 1904; deputy-registr. and appraiser, sup. ct., 1904; ag. registr., sup. ct., offl. admstr., offl. trustee, and registr. of companies, Mar. to Nov., 1907; ag. offl. recvr. in bank., Apr., 1907, to Apr., 1908; ag. 1st pol. mag., Apr., 1908 to June, 1909; head of san. dept., Nov., 1908; registr., sup. ct., offl. admstr., offl. trustee, and registr. of companies, 1909; crown solicitor, Jan., 1911; ag. puisne judge, Mar.-Nov., 1913; ag. atty.-gen., Mar., 1914.

KEMPE, Sir John Arrow, K.C.R. (1910), C.B. (1900), B.A. 1846; ed. St. Paul's Schl.
and Trin. Coll., Camb.; clk. treasv., 1867; priv. sec. to chanclr. of excheq., 1874-80, to Sir R. Lingen, 1880-81, to Lord F. Cavendish, 1881; mem. of coman. on agric. and dairy schls., 1887-88; prin. clk., treasv., 1888; dep. chmn., bd. of cust., 1894; mem. of royal coman. on elec. commun. with lighthouses and light vessels, 1892-97; asst. comptlr. and auditor, 1904; comptlr. and auditor-gen., 1905; hon. auditor of certain crown colonies and protectorates, ag. on behalf of S. of S. for the cols.; retired, 1911.

KEMPE, WILLIAM ALFRED.—Ed. at Haileybury Coll. and Trinity Coll., Camb.; B.A. (honours), 1903; col. audit branch of exchequer and audit dept., 10th Oct., 1904; temp. asst. auditor, E. Africa Prot., 2nd Oct., 1905; asst. auditor, 1st Sept., 1906; senr. asst. auditor, Apl., 1912.

KEEMPSFORD, GEORGE HENRY.—B. 1870; apptd., after exam., 3rd cls. messenger, C.O., 22nd Feb., 1904; 2nd cls., 1907.

KENNAN, THOMAS PONSONBY K.—Served in F.A.M.P. and C.M.R., 1877 to 1882, during Griqua and Basuto wars (medal); temporary clk. to R.M., Leribe, Basutoland, 1882; sub-inspr., Basuto pol., 1884; inspr., 1886; asst. comanr., Quathing, 1889.

KENNAWAY, SIR WALTER, KT. BACH. (1909), C.M.G. (1891).—Mem. prov. coun., Canterbury, N.Z., 1868-74; prov. sec. and sec. pub. wks., Cant., 1870-74; mem. bd. of educn., also bd. of govt., Cant. Coll.; 1873-4; sec., N.Z. govt. office, London, 1874 to 1899, when he retired; comanr., Col. and Ind. Exhibn., 1886; apptd. offir. of French Acad. for services at Paris Exhibn., 1889; ag. ast.-gen., 1891-1896; stock and loan agt. for N.Z. govt.; comanr. under N.Z. Pub. Rev. Acts.; custod. Pub. Trust Securities, London.
